registered.old: When a word like chicken has two trade meanings, the party claiming the narrower one has to prove it. Newcomers to a trade are bound by its usage only if they knew it or it was so settled they should have.
registered.new: When a word like chicken has two trade meanings, the plaintiff claiming the narrower one has to prove it. Under the New York law applied, newcomers to a trade are bound by its usage only if they knew it or it was so generally known that their knowledge could be inferred.
registered.reason: Friendly held that 'plaintiff has the burden of showing that "chicken" was used in the narrower rather than in the broader sense'; the newcomer rule he applied is New York law (actual knowledge, or a usage so generally known that knowledge may be inferred), and C&M Note 2 asks whether the Code would change the result.

registered.old: Under the UCC, trade usage and course of performance are part of the parties' agreement and may qualify an express term, such as a posted-price term, so long as they can reasonably be construed as consistent with it, without any showing of ambiguity.
registered.new: Under the UCC, trade usage of which the parties are or should be aware, and course of performance, are part of the agreement and may qualify an express posted-price term without a showing of ambiguity, if reasonably construed as consistent with it.

registered.old: Evidence of trade usage and past dealings comes in to explain a written sales contract unless it flatly cannot be squared with the express terms. The old rule that the writing first had to be ambiguous is gone under the Code.
registered.new: Evidence of trade usage and past dealings comes in to explain a written sales contract unless it cannot reasonably be construed as consistent with the express terms or the writing carefully negates it. The old rule that the writing first had to be ambiguous is gone under the Code.
registered.reason: Columbia Nitrogen's test is whether the evidence can 'reasonably be construed as consistent' with the express terms, unless carefully negated; 'flatly cannot be squared' lowers it.

registered.old: Identify this contract’s repeated performance, prior dealings, and sufficiently established trade usage. The buyer in Frigaliment failed to prove the narrow meaning of chicken. The rounding practice in Hurst could explain an apparently exact number.
registered.new: Identify this contract’s repeated performance, prior dealings, and sufficiently established trade usage. A usage counts against a party engaged in the trade or one who is or should be aware of it (UCC § 1-303(d)); under the New York law in Frigaliment, a newcomer is bound only by a usage it knew or one so generally known that its knowledge may be inferred. The buyer in Frigaliment failed to prove the narrow meaning of chicken. The rounding practice in Hurst could explain an apparently exact number.
registered.reason: The node sent any proved usage forward without asking whether it binds the party charged.
